description: gamut is an R geospatial package for exploring connections between United States cities and their water-supply catchments. The JOSS paper explains that land use, industry and other distant activities can affect urban water supply; the own README identifies the package and study setting. Spatial coverage is the cities and contributing catchments in the input data, and temporal coverage follows those source layers. The DESCRIPTION states BSD two-clause plus a licence file with Battelle terms, while GitHub classifies it as NOASSERTION. Link maps can inform water-supply interdependency or contamination-exposure simulations. A caveat is that a mapped catchment connection does not quantify pollutant transport, treatment performance or water reliability. Those mechanisms require separate models and observations. No directly related catalogue record was established. The article, own repository, DESCRIPTION and licence text were read without downloading catchment layers or running analysis.
